title: English: Reported Speech
source: Written for Henry (Nov 17-18): direct to reported, reported to direct, tense backshift, rules, relationship phrasal verbs, said or told. Concepts from his Unit 8 worksheet; new sentences. American spelling. Every question has a tier (easy, regular, hard, impossible) for Race Board; Quiz Battle ignores it. Written answers show one model answer; other correct versions are fine (that is optional).

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Tom said, "I am tired."
questions.answer: Tom said (that) he was tired.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Mia said, "I like this song."
questions.answer: Mia said (that) she liked that song.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: "We are playing soccer," the boys said.
questions.answer: The boys said (that) they were playing soccer.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Dad told me, "I will call you tomorrow."
questions.answer: Dad told me (that) he would call me the next day.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Anna said, "I have finished my homework."
questions.answer: Anna said (that) she had finished her homework.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: "I can swim," Ben said.
questions.answer: Ben said (that) he could swim.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Lisa said, "I went to Phuket yesterday."
questions.answer: Lisa said (that) she had gone to Phuket the day before.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: The teacher said to us, "Open your books."
questions.answer: The teacher told us to open our books.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Mom said to me, "Don't be late."
questions.answer: Mom told me not to be late.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: "Where do you live?" Sam asked me.
questions.answer: Sam asked me where I lived.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Ploy asked me, "Do you like pizza?"
questions.answer: Ploy asked me if (whether) I liked pizza.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Nok said, "I am going to study here tonight."
questions.answer: Nok said (that) she was going to study there that night.

questions.q: Change to direct speech: He said (that) he was hungry.
questions.answer: He said, "I am hungry."

questions.q: Change to direct speech: She said (that) she had lost her phone.
questions.answer: She said, "I have lost my phone." (or "I lost my phone.")

questions.q: Change to direct speech: They said (that) they would come the next day.
questions.answer: They said, "We will come tomorrow."

questions.q: Change to direct speech: Kim said (that) she could not find her keys.
questions.answer: Kim said, "I cannot find my keys."

questions.q: Change to direct speech: He said (that) he was reading a book then.
questions.answer: He said, "I am reading a book now."

questions.q: Change to direct speech: The doctor told me to rest.
questions.answer: The doctor said to me, "Rest!"

questions.q: Change to direct speech: She asked me where I lived.
questions.answer: She asked me, "Where do you live?"

questions.q: Change to direct speech: He asked me if I was ready.
questions.answer: He asked me, "Are you ready?"

questions.q: Change to direct speech: Mom told us not to run.
questions.answer: Mom said to us, "Don't run!"

questions.q: Change to direct speech: Jim said (that) he had seen the movie the week before.
questions.answer: Jim said, "I saw the movie last week." (or "I have seen the movie.")

questions.q: "I live in Bangkok." She said she ___ in Bangkok.
questions.answer: lived

questions.q: "I am cooking." He said he ___.
questions.answer: was cooking

questions.q: Past simple → past perfect: "I broke my phone." He said he ___ his phone.
questions.answer: had broken

questions.q: Past simple → past perfect: "We won the game." They said they ___ the game.
questions.answer: had won

questions.q: "I have finished." She said she ___ finished.
questions.answer: had

questions.q: "I will help you." He said he ___ help me.
questions.answer: would

questions.q: "I can speak French." She said she ___ speak French.
questions.answer: could

questions.q: Past continuous → past perfect continuous: "I was sleeping." He said he ___.
questions.answer: had been sleeping

questions.q: "I must go now." He said he ___ go then.
questions.answer: had to

questions.q: "I have been waiting for an hour." She said she ___ for an hour.
questions.answer: had been waiting

questions.q: "I am happy," she said. Which is correct?
choices: She said she has been happy.

questions.q: In reported speech, "tomorrow" usually becomes ___.
In reported speech, "yesterday" usually becomes ___.
In reported speech, "here" usually becomes ___.
The teacher ___ us to be quiet.
"Are you tired?" he asked. → He asked ___ I was tired.
"I have seen him." → She said she ___ him.
Which sentence is NOT correct?
choices: He asked me where I lived.
She said that she was busy.
He asked where did I live.

questions.q: Mint and Beam ___ after their argument. Now they are friends again.
I ___ really well with my sister. We never argue.
Last month Beam and Mint ___ about a secret. They did not talk for a week.
Ava's friends ___ her ___. They forgot her party.
I cannot ___ my neighbor's loud music any more.
It took Tom a week to ___ losing the soccer final.
Beam wants to ___ Mint ___ to the movies.
Let's ___ this weekend and watch a movie.
After two years, Sam and Pim decided to ___. They are not a couple now.
Which phrasal verb means "to end a romantic relationship"?
Which phrasal verb means "to accept something annoying without complaining"?
Mia and Ben have been ___ for six months. They are a couple.
She ___ me that she was tired.
questions.answer: told

questions.q: He ___ that he was busy.
questions.answer: said

questions.q: They ___ us the movie was great.
questions.answer: told

questions.q: Ruth ___ she understood.
questions.answer: said

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
choices: He said me that he was late.
He told me that he was late.
He told that he was late.
He said to that he was late.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
choices: She said me she was sorry.
She said to that she was sorry.

questions.q: The coach ___ the team to run faster.
questions.answer: told

questions.q: Nok ___ Ploy that she would call later.
questions.answer: told

questions.q: "Tell" is always followed by ___ (me, us, her...).
Fix the mistake: "He said me that he was hungry."
questions.answer: He told me that he was hungry. (or: He said that he was hungry.)

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Pim: "I am sorry."
questions.answer: Pim said (that) she was sorry.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Nat: "I can't come tonight."
questions.answer: Nat said (that) he couldn't (could not) come that night.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Gift: "I've made up with Fon."
questions.answer: Gift said (that) she had made up with Fon.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Mac: "I'm going to ask Jane out tomorrow."
questions.answer: Mac said (that) he was going to ask Jane out the next day.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Dan: "I'm watching a movie now."
questions.answer: Dan said (that) he was watching a movie then.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Bank: "I will get over it."
questions.answer: Bank said (that) he would get over it.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Fon: "We broke up last week."
questions.answer: Fon said (that) they had broken up the week before.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Jane: "I get on well with my brother."
questions.answer: Jane said (that) she got on well with her brother.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Pim told me: "I don't want to go out with him."
questions.answer: Pim told me (that) she didn't (did not) want to go out with him.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Nat: "My friends let me down yesterday."
questions.answer: Nat said (that) his friends had let him down the day before.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Gift: "We are getting together here on Friday."
questions.answer: Gift said (that) they were getting together there on Friday.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Mac: "I can't put up with this noise."
questions.answer: Mac said (that) he couldn't (could not) put up with that noise.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Ava asked me, "Why did you break up with him?"
questions.answer: Ava asked me why I had broken up with him.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Tom asked me, "Are you going to ask her out tomorrow?"
questions.answer: Tom asked me if (whether) I was going to ask her out the next day.
